notes.title: New campaign mechanics!
notes.content:
Hello!

I thought it'd be a great idea to share with you the new game mechanics I've been working on for the campaign for the last 3 weeks or so, as they are nearly ready for release!

The campaign was good for setting up staged battles but the resource harvesting, fleet management and strategic level control was not so great. 

The new campaign mode changes don't just affect campaign play, they affect everything about FtD and add two new strategic elements. 

The current tactical mode (press N, use "patrol AI cards") offers tactical control over the units.

A new mode has been added that allows assignment of vehicles into fleets, fleets can move and forces can be moved within the fleet into different formations (or your own custom formations).

The world map has been completely redone and now your fleets need to physically move from place to place (making a fleet of fast small boats much more viable than one single battleship). You'll need to spread your forces around your captured resource zones and intercept attackers. As a player character you can warp to any fleet on the map.

The map has also changed such that it is one continuous game world without any need for scene changes / load times. 

Obviously if the game world contains every AI fleet and every fleet you've ever made you'll be wondering what the "performance" is like! This brings me on to the next massive change: "in play" and "out of play" vehicles.

Prior to this development work battles could be so large that they'd cause extreme slow down (and even crash to desktop due to memory problems). With the new "out of play" mechanics all forces you are not interested in can be removed from play. These forces can still repair, harvest, smelt, grow crystal, move, etc, but don't use up and computational power and are not visible as vehicles. This makes fleet management extremely easy as you're dealing with "markers" not "vehicles".

Battles happen by moving fleets near each other on the map. Once within a certain range they enter "blockaded status" which means they cannot move or do anything. Once the player warps to the blockaded fleet and turns a force (or more) in play then the battle starts.

To keep battles manageable the campaign is kicked off with a "maximum number of blocks in play at any one time" parameter. This can be anywhere from 10K to 100K, depending on whether you want a more tactical game, or a more chaotic game, and also it allows those people with lower end machines to get a smooth experience.

The number of blocks you can spawn depends on the relative battling fleet sizes of you and your enemies (and your allies!). So if you bring 40 ships and they bring 5 ships then the game might have you spawning 8 against their 1 (five times over). So the balance of the forces is always fair (you had 8 times the number of ships that they did) but the game never loads in too many vehicles to play smoothly.

To make the game more user friendly you can now warp the player character directly from vehicle to vehicle, and even sit the player in an "out of play" vehicle and admire the view as it moves with the fleet.
 
As an example of the benefit this brings I quote the following functionality:
[list]
[*]Mass producing units painlessly by spawning in vehicles, turning them "out of play" and adding them to fleets with repair tentacles in them. You can go elsewhere and (assuming you have enough resource) when you come back they'll be at full health.
[*] Building resource miners in every resource zone, turning them out of play, and getting the full resource gathering, oil drilling, crystal farming, etc capability that you would if you were right there with them
[*] Creating fighter squadrons that can zip across the map and join you in battle, or watching an enemy battleship slowly lumber towards you across the map
[*] Managing dozens of vehicles in an out of play fleet, changing their formation and moving the fleet around without having to worry about them crashing into things!
[/list]


Fleets move at a speed determined by the forces within them, and have maximum altitudes. Top speed and maximum altitude need to be "proven" so when you build a new plane, take it for a spin to show the game what it can do. Save it as a blueprint and spawn another one and it'll automatically have the same top speed and maximum altitude.

Retrofitting will be added to FtD to allow a vehicle to be turned into another vehicle. If you build fleet of 30 bombers but then realise that you want each of them to have an extra missile launcher you can change one and "retrofit" all the others to the same standard using a simple GUI interface. 

These campaign changes also prepare FtD for trading mechanics and also a more complex resource mechanic where you need to actually transport resource around in order to spend it. Trading will definitely be added, and the resource mechanic will be an option that hardcore players can use.

Most importantly these campaign changes also make a co-op campaign mode very feasible for the future, so expect the co-op campaign somewhere near Christmas.

You can expect these new campaign mode features in the stable branch on Saturday the 8th of November. Old campaigns will be compatible with this mode but for the best experience I recommend starting the campaign again fresh!

Visit the official forum at www.fromthedepthsgame.com/forum for more details and I hope you're all enjoying the game !

Nick

This can be anywhere from 10K to 100K, depending on whether you want a more tactical game, or a more chaotic game, and also it allows those people with lower end machines to get a smooth experience.

The number of blocks you can spawn depends on the relative battling fleet sizes of you and your enemies (and your allies!). So if you bring 40 ships and they bring 5 ships then the game might have you spawning 8 against their 1 (five times over). So the balance of the forces is always fair (you had 8 times the number of ships that they did) but the game never loads in too many vehicles to play smoothly.

To make the game more user friendly you can now warp the player character directly from vehicle to vehicle, and even sit the player in an "out of play" vehicle and admire the view as it moves with the fleet.
 
As an example of the benefit this brings I quote the following functionality:
[list]
[*]Mass producing units painlessly by spawning in vehicles, turning them "out of play" and adding them to fleets with repair tentacles in them. You can go elsewhere and (assuming you have enough resource) when you come back they'll be at full health.
[*] Building resource miners in every resource zone, turning them out of play, and getting the full resource gathering, oil drilling, crystal farming, etc capability that you would if you were right there with them
[*] Creating fighter squadrons that can zip across the map and join you in battle, or watching an enemy battleship slowly lumber towards you across the map
[*] Managing dozens of vehicles in an out of play fleet, changing their formation and moving the fleet around without having to worry about them crashing into things!
[/list]


Fleets move at a speed determined by the forces within them, and have maximum altitudes. Top speed and maximum altitude need to be "proven" so when you build a new plane, take it for a spin to show the game what it can do. Save it as a blueprint and spawn another one and it'll automatically have the same top speed and maximum altitude.

Retrofitting will be added to FtD to allow a vehicle to be turned into another vehicle. If you build fleet of 30 bombers but then realise that you want each of them to have an extra missile launcher you can change one and "retrofit" all the others to the same standard using a simple GUI interface. 

These campaign changes also prepare FtD for trading mechanics and also a more complex resource mechanic where you need to actually transport resource around in order to spend it. Trading will definitely be added, and the resource mechanic will be an option that hardcore players can use.

Most importantly these campaign changes also make a co-op campaign mode very feasible for the future, so expect the co-op campaign somewhere near Christmas.

You can expect these new campaign mode features in the stable branch on Saturday the 8th of November. Old campaigns will be compatible with this mode but for the best experience I recommend starting the campaign again fresh!

Visit the official forum at www.fromthedepthsgame.com/forum for more details and I hope you're all enjoying the game !

Nick

notes.title: 1.531, 1.532,1.54,1.541,1.542 patch notes
notes.content:
[h1] Summary [/h1]
The main push with this series of updates was to get many more (30 or 40 more in fact) new community made designs into the game to represent the different factions of the game. You can see each faction in more detail [url=http://www.fromthedepthsgame.com/forum/forumdisplay.php?fid=30] here [/url]
A number of bugs have also been fixed and the main show stoppers in multiplayer have been fixed as well.


[h1] Bug fixes [/h1]

[bug fix] structures and fortresses now work in multiplayer
[bug fix] Password guess box is added when server is password protected
[bug fix] laser (simple) description updated to reflect that it uses ammo
[bug fix] capslock vehicle designer vehicle hold no longer slows down game for big vehicles
[bug fix] respawn beacon added to starting fortress, as well as some spare part crates
[bug fix] Saving vehicles in multiplayer no longer makes them 'enemy spawn' when loaded again
[bug fix] Precision spin block logic tightened up- they rotate in the same direction as normal spin blocks and their speed is correctly calculated.
[bug fix] bug fixes in the visualisation of prefabs before placement
[bug fix]Fortress controller moves fortress in orientation of fortress, not the controller placement
[bug fix]Shrinking blocks bug fixed for drills/laser components
[bug fix]Setting the rotation angle of a spin block via automatic control block does no longer revert 'rotation reverse' to 'rotation'
[bug fix]Some issues fixed with the selection of a vehicle of interest by looking at it
[bug fix]large block placement code fixed to allow, for example, jet engines to be placed more naturally
[bug fix]ammo,fuel,spares, reserve limits are saved to the constructable
[bug fix]Scuttlebot death in MP is fixed

[h1] Features [/h1]
You can now select the team when spawning a vehicle in the designer

Vehicle designer freeze vehicle button (CAPS LOCK by default) is customisable (CAPS LOCK does not work on MAC in Unity)

Many in game vehicles added and many updated, each faction now has multiple different unique units.

Custom missile staggered fire is now more robust for second salvo 

Wood can be placed at multiple orientations, as it could be before 1.53

You will save the vehicle you are building on, when in build mode, regardless of the vehicle you are actually standing on or closest to.

The firing delay for weapons is now enabled

Explosive missile warheads now stack into a single larger explosion

There is a configurable delay on the automatic control block trigger pulse

Changes to the way blueprints spawn in campaign mode

[h1] What's next [/h1]
[url=http://www.fromthedepthsgame.com/forum/showthread.php?tid=1981] See here for more info[/url]

notes.title: 1.52 and 1.53 series change log
notes.content:
Hi there :)

The main idea here was to get a working multiplayer co-op designer mode. That goal was achieved but there is still a lot of work to do on the multiplayer aspects of the game.

I've also added new engine art and implemented a new way of rendering alloy and metal blocks using a seamless tileable texture that covers a 4x4 area of blocks. 

The multiplayer creative mode is not yet finished but is playable and open to everyone to test. A large number of blocks only work currently on the server side, and "join in progress" not yet added.


[h1] Summary [/h1]
Multiplayer creative mode, corner blocks and alloy and metal textures look much nicer.

[h1] Bug fixes [/h1]

[Bug fix] Laser transceiver connectivity bug fixed
[Bug fix] Laser firing through terrain bug fixed
[bug fix] Shells from autocannon inherit platform velocity
[bug fix] patrols to -1,-1 are now re-tasked
[bug fix] Resource no longer given for removing dead blocks
[bug fix]Crash fixed when deleting turret/spinner whilst building on it in simple build mode
[bug fix] enemies spawned in from vehicle load GUI as enemy AI will still be treated as salvage
[bug fix] connecting transceivers into turrets bug fixed
[bug fix] single player respawn bug fix from last version
[bug fix] wood pieces that the resource gatherer digs up are now low poly- performance improvements.
[bug fix] Campaign diplomatic relations reset after new game start
[bug fix] Campaign time reset after starting a new game. No more shrike bombers as first attack on a second play through
[bug fix] radar does not give the appearance of working when it is disconnected

[h1] Features [/h1]
Multiplayer hosting and joining settings are saved
Auto login to last used player profile
Multiplayer co-op vehicle designer mode added
Drive maintained positive plus negative inputs together stop the drive
Build mode double tap speeds up cursor in all directions (not just W)
Simple build mode can now paint as well
Story mission select GUI prompts player to buy some resource
The 'attack salvage' option is now saved to the AI mainframe
Naval AI idle approach distance (default 50 metres) is now configurable
Suicide pill item added
Engine art completely overhauled
Art style changed for alloy and metal blocks- seamless alloy and metal pieces
new corner blocks added for alloy, metal and wood
prefab placing now shows the blocks you are going to place
prefab selection marker now more clearly shows the extent of the prefab to be selected
you can fill with larger blocks
		
[h1] What's next [/h1]

A long over due addition of content to the single player campaign, the first boss fight of the story missions and fixing any bugs that will come up in the multiplayer creative mode, whilst adding all the rest of the features the multiplayer needs.

notes.title: 1.51 series changelog
notes.content:
In v1.51 a lot of time went into creating a building control system that would be immediately familiar to new players. Press F3 to toggle between the different building controls and I highly recommend sticking with the original mode as it offers a much higher level of precision once you learn to use it. The original build controls have also been improved in this update and you can now use keys to rotate the building orientation. Lots of different options have been opened up on the "Options menu" to allow you to select the build mode that works best for you.

Fuel injected custom jet engines have also been added but are still in development- they work but are not very well balanced at this early stage.

Multiplayer connectivity issues have been fixed which means you can play the basic multiplayer mode. No new developments on the co-op vehicle designer have been made yet.

A "knowledge base" replaces the tutorial portion of the game- it has many video links, links to the building guide, the tutorial, skirmish missions, forums and wiki

A bunch of other useful things have been added for example you can now control the tail rotor of a helicopter by setting it into "instant spin" mode where it will only spin when you have the appropriate button pressed. This could also be used for spinning melee weapons.

You can now hold shift to speed up the camera x4 in free look mode and hold E when the orbit camera is being used to freeze the camera- very useful for setting up weapons via their GUI interface.

[h1] Full change log [/h1]

Look based building controls added to game, similar to other voxel games for those that like that sort of thing

Standard build mode now allows you to control orientation of block using TAB + WASDQE

Fixed a bug regarding trying to paint after selecting a prefab

Failsafe cylinder length and radius is now configurable via a GUI

Laser destabiliser now connects properly

Tutorial page turned into a full "Knowledge base" with all sorts of links to various pieces of information

Missile warner no longer picks up torpedos or other missiles that are in the water

Laser in pulse mode can destroy multiple blocks

Laser cavities no longer connect sideways

Prefabs are loaded with the color index they were saved with

You can freeze the rotation of the orbit camera in GUIs by holding 'E'

Missiles on turrets wont fire until they are within the missile controller's 'required accuracy before fire' value of the target

You can no longer build on enemy turrets

Maximum fire rate of AI set to be as fast as possible

Fuel injected jet engines added quite possibly buggy at this stage!)

Connectivity issues with the standard dedicated master server fixed

Proxy based connection option added to increase connectivity yet again, at expense of latency

[1.511] Spinners can have a variable rotation speed allowing for touch control of helicopters

[1.511] Hold shift in free view mode to speed up camera x4

[1.511] AI wireless equipment made more expensive and physical connectors made less expensive

[1.511] Maximum radius for explosive shells capped at 10 metres

[h1] What's next? [/h1]

Adding more content to the campaign, more built in vehicles, a new story mission featuring a nasty boss battle and the co-op designer multiplayer mode. Look forward to hearing your thoughts on this update and what should come next!

notes.title: v1.50 change log
notes.content:
v1.50 focuses on adding guides for new players (and experienced players)- you can now follow step by step on-rails guides for building all of the main component types. They are accessible from the main menu and during play in the vehicle designer. There are a bunch of other minor tweaks and bug fixes as well.

[h1] Full change log [/h1]

Player experience and level always saved now

Building guide for engines, cannons, missiles, electric engines, AI, sails, planes, boats, lasers, resource gathering/processing all added

you can spray paint through shields now

Tractor beamed vehicles don't get damaged by collisions

Fixed bug with sonar and one turn component

Splash noises added

Game prompts you to save before quitting in campaign

Input manager had a duplicate entry for rolling left and right, now fixed

F9 is now for HUD toggle and F12 is for screenshots

Made it a bit more obvious how to equip a skill in character sheet

[1.501] laser transceivers only connect to one other transceiver. Same as before but they'll choose the closest

[1.501] Camera splash noises removed in build mode

[1.501] Rain volume reduced

[1.501] A prompt added telling you how to edit a turret- more functionality to be added later"

[h1] What's next [/h1]

I want to add a few more components of the course of the next few days- the fuel injected jet engines, a anchor and a barrage balloon. The barrage balloon is a balloon with a thick wire attaching it to the vehicle. The idea is that if a plane (such as a bomber) hits the wire then it will be cut in half... the faster the plane is going the more damage it takes. These will I hope help to even the odds with planes vs. ships!

notes.title: Change log of v1.490,1.491 and 1.492
notes.content:
Here is the change log for changes made on Sun through Thursday. The campaign now has a special fleet, missiles revert to default builds when first made and you can save/copy and paste large chunks (or prefabs) or your vehicles around. A lot of these changes are to make the game more accessible to new players (and to allow more complete customisation of keys). Lots of new sounds, two new components added and there's also a few bug fixes in there (all reported bugs are I believe now fixed)! Read the full log below:

[h1] Full change log [/h1]

Default heat seeking missiles are built for you when you 3, 4 or 5 missile blocks on a launch pad. Add a laser block to the missile battery and the missiles will default to laser designated missiles.

Button added to missile edit menu to flow a design to all same length missiles on the controller

A copy / paste function has been added allowing the saving and loading of 'prefabs'. Check the prefabs section of the inventory for some default prefabs. This is particularly of use to new players.

Resource zones and your fleets displayed on the tactical map when you are returning to a location or engaging enemy territory

The WASD binding for the character (which is customisable) has been extended to build mode. So you can now customise build mode

Left and right click for using player items can be re-bound elsewhere- so can the vehicle fire buttons

you can now change the 'desired minimum FPS' to allow it to run at normal 1:1 speed but with low FPS, or visa versa

[1.491] Rams should now give experience, and drills should give experience 100% of the time (bug fix)

[1.491] Special fleet DWG Shrike Bomber squad added to campaign

[1.491] Missile component 'camera' added for selecting a range of targets for heat seekers

[1.491] An AI Failsafe block has been added to attach to a local weapon controller to stop it shooting parts of your ship

[1.491] Fixed a bug with the damage system that may have caused a few campaigns and blueprints to be come unsaveable (bug fix)

[1.491] Added more sounds to the game (ship noises, turret noises and shield projector hum)

[1.492] Blocks fall off in 'freeze vehicle mode' (bug fix)

[1.492] Suppression barrel no longer removes all recoil (bug fix)

[1.492] Sub objects, when placed, now charge resource (bug fix)

[1.492] Info for low experience level players displayed on main menu
			
[1.492] Bug fixed with engine exhaust where it was mistaken for fuel tank. (bug fix)

[h1] What's next [/h1]

The weekend's focus will be on more (and better) tutorials, adding more content to the campaign and adding customisable fuel injected jet engines. A health bar might make it's way in as well!

notes.title: v1.481 to 1.484 change log
notes.content:
A number of changes have been made since the launch on steam- these are listed below!

[h1] Summary [/h1] You can now freeze your vehicle in the designer with capslock and I've added "elevation only" cannon barrels for more realistic battleship-like turrets as well as radar antennas and radar dishes for long range searches on the strategic map. In addition I've added the first story mission for the Onyx Watch campaign. In this campaign you play as a war-technician and in mission 1 you're defending a scrap processing plant from bombing raids.

[h1] Full change log [/h1]

[1.481] More depth to not being at war with teams in campaign- those you are not at war with are counted as neutral and won't attack you. Damaging them hurts your relationship with their fraction.


[1.481] Fixed the ships wheel for spinning the masts- was doing it the wrong way

[1.481] Added diplomacy menu to campaign menu sidebar- incase you forget the key (F1)

[1.481] Fixed a number of small inventory based bugs

[1.482] Mouse invert is now working

[1.482] Radar antenna and dish components added, for campaign mode, but not yet functional

[1.482] Tightened up the turrets a bit to make them sway around a bit less.

[1.482] Stoped the scuttbot camera moving by accident

[1.482] AI cannon aiming against moving targets has been improved

[1.482] New Story mission added for the Onyx watch- defending your scrap processing plants from bomber raids!

[1.483] Press CAPSLOCK in build mode to freeze the vehicle in designer mode

[1.483] Shadows added to 'fantastic' and 'beautiful' render mode

[1.483] Elevation only barrel added for AA guns and artillery

[1.484] Fixed the Onyx watch story mission to make it winnable

[1.484] Seeking missile launcher no longer takes ammo if cannot fire

[1.485] Fixed bug with electric engines and spelling mistake

[h1] What's next [/h1]

Look back at the previous change logs for a longer term development plan- but the focus for the next day or so will be adding prefab loading and saving for chunks of the blueprint, adding default functional missiles (so a newly placed missile is of a reasonable standard rather than being 100% empty body modules) and perhaps offering some different and more familiar build mechanics for those coming into FTD from other games.

In addition I've added the first story mission for the Onyx Watch campaign. In this campaign you play as a war-technician and in mission 1 you're defending a scrap processing plant from bombing raids.

[h1] Full change log [/h1]

[1.481] More depth to not being at war with teams in campaign- those you are not at war with are counted as neutral and won't attack you. Damaging them hurts your relationship with their fraction.


[1.481] Fixed the ships wheel for spinning the masts- was doing it the wrong way

[1.481] Added diplomacy menu to campaign menu sidebar- incase you forget the key (F1)

[1.481] Fixed a number of small inventory based bugs

[1.482] Mouse invert is now working

[1.482] Radar antenna and dish components added, for campaign mode, but not yet functional

[1.482] Tightened up the turrets a bit to make them sway around a bit less.

[1.482] Stoped the scuttbot camera moving by accident

[1.482] AI cannon aiming against moving targets has been improved

[1.482] New Story mission added for the Onyx watch- defending your scrap processing plants from bomber raids!

[1.483] Press CAPSLOCK in build mode to freeze the vehicle in designer mode

[1.483] Shadows added to 'fantastic' and 'beautiful' render mode

[1.483] Elevation only barrel added for AA guns and artillery

[1.484] Fixed the Onyx watch story mission to make it winnable

[1.484] Seeking missile launcher no longer takes ammo if cannot fire

[1.485] Fixed bug with electric engines and spelling mistake

[h1] What's next [/h1]

Look back at the previous change logs for a longer term development plan- but the focus for the next day or so will be adding prefab loading and saving for chunks of the blueprint, adding default functional missiles (so a newly placed missile is of a reasonable standard rather than being 100% empty body modules) and perhaps offering some different and more familiar build mechanics for those coming into FTD from other games.

notes.title: v1.47 and v1.48 change log
notes.content:
It's been a hectic few days preparing for the launch (it launches at v1.481).. and so here are all the changed that have gone in.

[h1] Summary [/h1]
The main change is the addition of diplomacy to the single player campaign, you can declare war, insult, bribe, turn on your allies, and incite war between other factions. Enemy fleets now have a whole range of peace and war time activities. A lot of clarification of the components in the inventory has also been added and a bunch of bug fixes. The other significant change is that the Miner attribute affects gameplay, and a smelter and crystal farm components have been added to help you grow and transform your resource. Custom cannons have been balanced a bit to make the smaller ones more useful.

[h1] Full change log [/h1]
Campaign locked until experience level 4

Square rig sail is unlocked by winning a story mission, as is sailing AI card

Tutorial video is linked in to tutorial menu

Tutorial and skirmish missions updated to use new character avatars

Selected component name now displayed on HUD... HUD tidied up a bit

AI will control your weapons when you are in build mode

players made weightless (almost) when in chairs

[1.471] Miner attribute affects game-play

[1.471] Scrap smelter parts added for making scrap resource

[1.471] Crystal farm added

[1.471] Faction / player relationships added in campaign mode

[1.471] A lot of new faction fleet activities added

[1.471] New starting fortress in single player campaign

[1.471] Capturing resource zones from enemy slows their advancement

[1.471] Foot latch re-enabled for scuttlebot

[1.471] Rotations of blocks in multiplayer always correct now

[1.48] Key map updated (options-->controls)

[1.48]Inventory descriptions updated for many components",
		
[1.48]Got the remote controller and control terminal working once again (works nicely now!)

[1.48]Updated the tractor-beam/docking station so that player doesn't glitch through held vehicles",

[1.48]Batteries save and load their charge (and are emptied when appropriate)

[1.48]Same for fuel storage, engine fuel tank and ammo barrel",

[1.48]Added friendly fire to campaign to affect relationships- so you can declare war by shooting on allies.",

[1.48]Two factions that are not at war in campaign will not fight each other",

[1.48]Tidied up repair and attack decision making

[1.48]Laser defense block will no longer damage friendlies that get in the way

[1.48]Fleets no longer get stuck trying to fortify a board section

[1.48]Repair bugs will repair blocks on turrets and spin blocks from long ranges

[1.48]Repair code tightened up
			
[1.48]Custom cannons now no longer benefit exponentially from being bigger

[1.48]Enemy fleet numbers increased in campaign mode

[[1.481] More depth to not being at war with teams in campaign

[1.481] Fixed the ships wheel for spinning the masts- was doing it the wrong way

[1.481] Added diplomacy menu to campaign menu sidebar- in case you forget the key (F1)

[1.481] Fixed a number of small inventory based bugs"


[b] What's next [/b]

I'm tempted to get stuck straight into multiplayer, leaving the new fuel fed jet engines (that I hinted at in the last update) for another update. I will also be adding custom fleets to the campaign so you will have to face specific and rather nasty opponents once in a while! Assuming multiplayer development goes well there will be a multiplayer creative mode at some point soon! I'm also tempted by adding strategic radar components to spot fleets on the strategic map in the campaign mode.These will be huge dished (made up of lots of smaller parts) ideally placed on a spin block, on a hill somewhere!

As always I look forward to your thoughts and suggestions!

notes.title: v1.46 - change log
notes.content:
At time of writing this v1.46 has come and gone (1.47 was released a moment ago), consisting of a major update and four minor ones. Let's recap on what changed!

[h1] Summary [/h1]
The main additions are the inclusions of customisable laser components, and missile defence and player attributes that affect gameplay. Many bug fixes and UI improvements were also included. Another story mission has been added that makes use of some (new) drill components and the story missions now unlock a few high end components when you complete them.

[h1]Here is the (almost) full change log.[/h1]
Bugs introduced in one sub version and fixed in the next are not shown.

Various AI components can be placed on turrets and connector via wireless link to the mainframe
Laser components added and Missile warning Ai component added
Fixed bug with rambot control of nearby weapons and controllers
Melee attack now possible without an item equipped

[1.461] Fixed rotation of new fortresses and vehicles placed
[1.461] Fixed miss-identification of some laser parts when looked at
[1.461] AI sets to on when combat mode is not available
[1.461] Fixed some issues with the rambot avatar getting stuck
[1.461] New story mission added for deep water guard
[1.461] Lasers now shoot through shields (both directions)
[1.461] Inventory item buttons updated
[1.461] Unlocks added to game
[1.461] large block buoyancy corrected
[1.461] drill extension sideways connects added
		
			
[1.462] The mechanic skill now affects gameplay!
[1.462] Repair code tightened up for player's tentacles
[1.462] Spares use enabled during repairs
[1.462] Grenade launcher fixed
[1.462] Spares crate added

[1.463] Changing fleet colors on character sheet updates them in game
[1.463] Character sheet button (Normally Z) is remappable for German / European players
[1.463] Graphical glitch in save sub-constructable inventory tab GUI fixed

[1.464] Fixed chairs so you can't accidentally jump out
[1.464] Added alt to move downwards so you can control yourself in space better (both avatars)",
[1.464] Sky captain & Space captain attribute affects gameplay

[h1] What's next [/h1]
In the 1.47 series of updates I hope to refine further the single player campaign, adding a "quest log" of sorts, as well as some player-->faction relations and linking the faction economy to their captured assets. I also have a back log of dozens of community made vehicles to incorporate into the campaign

[h1] What's after that [/h1]
I'm 50% of the way towards customisable jet engines (think 30 metre long fuel guzzling contraptions consisting of air intakes, compressors, combusters, exhausts, after burners, etc). They're looking great and I hope to get them into the game ASAP. No more plastering the back wall of a plane with "huge jet" components and having to build a huge traditional engine to power it. 
I also have plans for a series of custom cannon components allowing ammo to be stored up and either belt fed to produce a fully auto or bust fire, or loaded up and fired in a shotgun like multi-shell burst. 
And of course another main priority is the incorporation of the player character into multiplayer, to facilitate a multiplayer creative mode.

As always your ideas and thoughts are extremely welcome!
